brief: Rising global yields are hitting fixed income and credit broadly: bond volatility sits near YTD highs, all major US fixed-income sectors are now negative YTD, and France's 10-year yield topped 4.9% (highest since 2002) with its OAT-Bund spread at 129bps, widest since the 2012 European debt crisis. Credit stress concentrates at the bottom: CCC spreads broke 1,000bps (first since March 2023, +450bps since February) and the CCC-BB gap is widest since 2020; high-yield widened to 318bps but stays below its March peak. RJ favors higher-quality credit, with IG spreads near 80bps and yields above 6%. Ahead of today's payrolls, mixed signals (weak JOLTS, sub-200k claims, falling Challenger cuts) point to a low-hire, low-fire labor market; RJ forecasts a 70k print. Despite the 10-year above 5.3%, the S&P 500 fell just 0.5% in September, but breadth is collapsing: the equal-weight index faces a 7th straight weekly decline and 43% of constituents are in a bear market, so RJ expects narrow leadership until yields stabilize. The dollar, up 3.7% YTD, looks stretched to RJ: it tracks oil amid the Iran conflict (a drop could spark profit-taking) and is priced for nearly four Fed hikes versus RJ's own call of one more.
